name: EgoZero
summary: EgoZero takes the human-data idea to its limit: collect demonstrations with Aria glasses, extract a morphology-agnostic state and action representation built from 3D points rather than images or joint angles, train a policy on that alone, and deploy on a gripper robot that contributed nothing to training. Reported results cover several everyday manipulation tasks from a few minutes of human recording each.
innovation: A point-based, morphology-agnostic state and action representation that erases the embodiment gap by construction rather than by learning around it.
Transfer to a real robot with literally no robot training data.
matters: If this scales it removes teleoperation from the pipeline entirely, which is the single largest cost in the field.
limits: Small task set, short horizons and coarse precision; wholly dependent on accurate hand and object tracking.
lineage: EgoMimic's alignment idea pushed until robot data is no longer required at all.
